data.title: Cutaneous candidiasis / intertrigo — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Cutaneous candidiasis / intertrigo** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Causative organism?**
- Candida albicans (commonest), C. tropicalis, C. parapsilosis, C. glabrata, C. krusei; emerging C. auris (multidrug-resistant)

**Q2. Predisposing factors?**
- Moisture/occlusion (obesity, skin folds, diapers), diabetes, pregnancy, broad-spectrum antibiotics, steroids, immunosuppression (HIV), infancy and old age, dentures, iron deficiency, endocrinopathies

**Q3. Clinical forms?**
- Intertrigo: moist beefy-red plaques with peripheral scaling and satellite papulopustules in folds
- Oral thrush, angular cheilitis, vulvovaginitis, balanoposthitis, napkin candidiasis, chronic paronychia, onychomycosis, erosio interdigitalis blastomycetica (3rd web space of hand), chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis

**Q4. How to differentiate from tinea cruris?**
- Candida: involves scrotum, beefy red, satellite pustules, no central clearing; tinea cruris spares scrotum, active scaly border with central clearing

**Q5. Investigations?**
- KOH: budding yeast with pseudohyphae; Gram stain; culture on Sabouraud's (creamy colonies), germ tube test (C. albicans), CHROMagar species ID
- Blood sugar, HIV in recurrent/extensive cases

**Q6. What is chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis?**
- Persistent candida of skin, nails and mucosa from defective IL-17 immunity — AIRE mutation (APECED: hypoparathyroidism, Addison disease), STAT1 gain-of-function, STAT3 (hyper-IgE)

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Keep area dry; topical azoles (clotrimazole, miconazole), nystatin, ciclopirox; drying agents/barrier pastes
- Systemic: fluconazole 150 mg weekly or 50–100 mg daily × 2 weeks; itraconazole for resistant species (C. krusei is resistant to fluconazole)
- Treat predisposing causes (weight loss, glycaemic control)

## Quick spotter facts
- Beefy red moist plaque in the inframammary fold with satellite pustules — candidal intertrigo

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Superficial fungal infection — candidiasis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.18. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
